evidence.why: Non-const table, state selections and callback mutations.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unsupported immutable characterization while preserving the supported dispatch and per-item data-flow explanation.
facts.value: Motion-state indices 0 and 1 select callback triplets from the two-entry ItemStateTable. The registered callbacks operate on each supplied item's velocity, facing, collision data and Kinoko working fields; no table mutation occurs in this unit. The array is declared without const, so these observations do not establish immutability or compiled read-only placement.

facts.rationale: Removes the misleading private characterization; the canonical definition is non-static and the module header exposes its declaration.
facts.value: Item landing and motion-state entry callback with signature void(Item_GObj* gobj), defined with external linkage and declared in itkinoko.h. It mutates the Item attached to the supplied game object and returns no result.

evidence.why: Distinct accessor and per-instance movement paths, including cached-speed lifetime.
Returned animation is installed on the fighter helper joint and consumed for scaling.

facts.rationale: Separates the fighter animation-resource path from item movement rather than implying that animation data feeds facing and collision vectors.
facts.value: The unit has separate movement and transformation-resource paths. Spawn X position determines item facing; Kinoko speed and drag attributes plus common falling attributes drive velocity. Per-instance kinoko.x0 caches signed travel speed and kinoko.x4 caches surface geometry across grounded physics, collision, ground loss and landing; airborne drag changes current horizontal velocity without updating the cached speed. Independently, it_80293660 returns KinokoAnim[idx + 2].joint from the global Kinoko article, and fighter code installs that animation on a helper JObj whose animated X scale drives interpolation between fighter scale endpoints.
